hypothesis: At fixed translation and unchanged textured surround/360-degree yaw endpoints, reducing angular rate fourfold will delay or prevent the early VINS health lock seen in r20 if angular rate is the dominant cause.
single_primary_variable: yaw angular rate (angular acceleration reduced sixteenfold to preserve the same full-turn endpoints over four times the phase duration)

observed.stop: docker stop --timeout 15; outer runner ended with exit code 137. mapping-stack.log remained on the shared volume; recorder/motion finalizers did not complete before the container was killed.
observed.qualification: VINS pose quaternion is extracted from mapping-stack.log (wxyz order); it is an estimator output, not independent motion truth.

interpretation: The first logged zero feature-count frame occurred at estimated yaw about 0.61 degrees, but the first mapping health-gate closure followed 28.38 simulation seconds later at estimated yaw about 16.37 degrees. The failure was delayed relative to r20 (health closure at sim 13.564 seconds and estimated yaw 2.43 degrees), yet localization did not remain valid to the end of the 360-degree scan. The slow-rate hypothesis is therefore only partially supported: rate affected onset timing, but this scan still failed its positive-entry criterion.

next_hypothesis.primary_variable: insert a stationary reacquisition hold after each rest-to-rest 15-degree yaw segment, keeping the same surround, stationary translation and approximately the same peak angular rate as r21.
next_hypothesis.rationale: r21 had isolated feature-count zero events well before persistent mapping health lock. Short scan-and-hold segments test whether a fixed view lets feature tracks and health recover before the next yaw increment.
next_hypothesis.stop_method: On health lock, SIGINT the sensor-motion process group inside the container; let the container cleanup SIGINT the input recorder and mapping stack so both write partial artifacts. The host cleanup now allows 90 seconds before container kill.
